judgment_methodology.method: MQM (Multidimensional Quality Metrics) error typology to classify a translation defect's severity
judgment_methodology.source: Lommel et al., MQM framework (2014); themqm.org

planning_methodology.method: ISO 17100 translation-project workflow (preparation, translation, revision, review, proofreading)

deliverable_form.method: XLIFF 2.1 translatable-unit package with locale metadata

feedback_methodology.method: MQM-scored bilingual review with per-error severity weighting
feedback_methodology.source: Lommel et al., MQM framework (2014); themqm.org

review_methodology.method: ISO 17100 revision-and-review step performed by a second linguist against the source

reference_resolution.rule: locale must resolve to an actual CLDR locale identifier — no orphan references (issue-515 invariant 2).

recomputation.rule: pattern_value is recomputed by re-validating it against the locale's current LDML pattern grammar, never a standalone asserted field.
recomputation.checked_by: TBD (follow-up — issue-521 out-of-scope note: per-role recomputation enforcement is a follow-up once evidence from real usage shows which roles need it)

quality_bar.verification_method: automated check that `pattern_value` parses under the LDML pattern grammar for its declared `pattern_type` and `locale`, matching the spec's own `recomputation` rule
quality_bar.verified_source: Unicode, 'UTS #35: Unicode LDML' — https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr35/ (primary source; §Date/Time/Number Format Patterns define the exact per-type grammar a pattern_value must satisfy).

quality_bar.verification_method: human-review-checklist: is any translated string assembled by concatenating separately-translated word fragments (rather than translating a whole sentence/phrase as one unit)?
quality_bar.verified_source: Unicode, 'UTS #35: Unicode LDML', 'MessageFormat' section — https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr35/#Message_Format (primary source; LDML's own message-format design exists specifically to avoid fragment concatenation, since word order and inflection are not universal across locales).

quality_bar.verification_method: human-review-checklist: is every flagged translation defect classified with an MQM error category and severity (minor/major/critical), rather than left as an unclassified note?
quality_bar.verified_source: Lommel et al., 'Multidimensional Quality Metrics (MQM)' — https://themqm.org (primary source; MQM's own framework requires each error to carry a typed category and severity weight, matching the spec's own `feedback_methodology`).

quality_bar.verification_method: automated check that a revision/review step by a second linguist (distinct from the original translator) is recorded before the pattern is marked `validating`, matching the spec's own `review_methodology`
quality_bar.verified_source: ISO 17100:2015, 'Translation services — Requirements for translation services' — iso.org/standard/59149.html (primary source; ISO 17100 mandates a revision step performed by a person other than the translator as a required stage, not optional QA).

quality_bar.verification_method: gates/quality_bar.py:human_comprehensibility_verdict against the role's own docs/issue-<n>/reports/<role>.md record text (gates/human_comprehensibility.py tier-1 structural prose rules: lead paragraph present, citation trailing placement, section size bound, no raw dump, enumeration cap); a record with no human-facing prose section anywhere is exempt (bar-met) -- issue #1623.

use_when.board_condition: a new locale or translated string lands on the branch AND no localization record exists yet for that locale
